bibliographic.title: Reporting guideline for chatbot health advice studies: the Chatbot Assessment Reporting Tool (CHART) statement
bibliographic.citation_apa: The CHART Collaborative. (2025). Reporting guideline for chatbot health advice studies: the Chatbot Assessment Reporting Tool (CHART) statement. BMJ Medicine, 4. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjmed-2025-001632

methodology.method_family: reporting guideline development via systematic review, modified asynchronous Delphi consensus, and expert panel consensus meetings
methodology.study_design: multi-phase guideline development (systematic review, Delphi, consensus meetings, pilot testing)
methodology.sample_description: 531 international stakeholders in Delphi consensus; 48 members in expert panel consensus meetings
methodology.technology_context: generative AI-driven chatbots and large language models used for summarising clinical evidence and providing health advice (chatbot health advice studies)

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article develops CHART, a reporting guideline—not an empirical study of conversational governance in deployed LLM systems. It is highly relevant as foundational context for transparent evaluation and reporting of generative-AI chatbot health advice studies, including ethics, disclosures, model identifiers, and harm-related appraisal, but does not directly address operational governance mechanisms such as guardrails, observability, audit logs, human oversight workflows, or post-deployment monitoring.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial methods text were provided; full checklist items, limitations, and development-phase details require full-text verification.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal based on abstract and introductory/methods excerpts only. Guideline-development methods (systematic review, Delphi with 531 stakeholders, 48-member expert panel) are clearly described; limitations of CHART itself are not visible in the supplied text.

cerqual.explanation: Method development appears coherent and adequately described in the excerpt, but supplied text is incomplete for full critical appraisal. Relevance to conversational governance is indirect: the paper standardises reporting of chatbot health advice studies rather than prescribing governance controls for regulated conversational AI deployment.

coding.theme: Standardised reporting for generative-AI chatbot health advice studies
coding.subtheme: Transparency, ethics, and methodological disclosure as enablers of appraisal and trust

synthesis.main_claim: CHART is a 12-item reporting guideline developed to promote transparent and comprehensive reporting of studies evaluating generative-AI-driven chatbots that summarise clinical evidence and provide health advice.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a structured checklist and methodological diagram for chatbot health advice studies, developed from a systematic review, Delphi consensus among 531 stakeholders, and expert panel meetings; includes reporting items on model details, prompt engineering, query strategy, performance evaluation, ethics, protocol, and data availability.
synthesis.limitations: Supplied text does not report CHART's own limitations, validation scope beyond pilot testing, or applicability outside healthcare chatbot advice studies; operational governance of deployed conversational systems is not addressed.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence on reporting standards and transparency expectations for LLM/chatbot health advice research; cite when discussing appraisal frameworks, ethics disclosure, and methodological rigour in regulated healthcare conversational AI studies, not as central evidence on operational conversational governance.

evidence.claim: Peer-reviewed journal article in BMJMED 2025 with stated DOI.
Study type is methodological reporting guideline development for generative-AI chatbot health advice studies.
evidence.excerpt: The Chatbot Assessment Reporting Tool (CHART) is a reporting guideline developed to provide reporting recommendations for studies evaluating the performance of generative artificial intelligence (AI)-driven chatbots

evidence.claim: Development combined systematic review, Delphi consensus, and expert panel meetings.
evidence.excerpt: CHART was developed in several phases after performing a comprehensive systematic review
revised through an international, multidisciplinary, modified, asynchronous Delphi consensus process of 531 stakeholders

evidence.claim: Expert panel comprised 48 members in consensus meetings.
evidence.excerpt: three synchronous panel consensus meetings of 48 stakeholders

evidence.claim: CHART contains 12 items and 39 subitems covering ethics and disclosures.
Reporting items include ethics, protocol, and data availability.
evidence.excerpt: disclosures (subitem 12a), funding (subitem 12b), ethics (subitem 12c), protocol (subitem 12d), and data availability (subitem 12e)

evidence.claim: Technology context explicitly involves LLMs and generative AI chatbots.
evidence.excerpt: With the introduction of large language models (LLMs) into mainstream use

evidence.claim: Regulated healthcare domain with risk of patient harm highlighted.
evidence.excerpt: raise the risk of patient harm, particularly if generative AI-driven models are used for health purposes

evidence.claim: Transparent reporting linked to critical appraisal and trust.
evidence.excerpt: Complete and standardised reporting facilitates critical appraisal and may help to identify applications with genuine potential to improve healthcare, building trust

evidence.claim: CHA studies use chat-based interfaces to query generative AI models.
evidence.excerpt: Investigators typically develop prompts to query generative AI models through a chat based interface

evidence.claim: LLM defined as subset of generative AI in glossary.
evidence.excerpt: Large language model (LLM) A type of AI model comprising large neural networks trained over large amounts of text

evidence.claim: Generative-AI chatbot defined as user interaction with an AI model such as an LLM.
evidence.excerpt: Generative AI-driven chatbot A programme that permits users to interact with an AI model (such as an LLM) designed to respond to user prompts

evidence.claim: Reporting incompleteness is a documented problem in CHA studies.
evidence.excerpt: the completeness of reporting among these studies has been highly variable
